extracted.intended_audience: Federal Register users, regulated parties, agency officials, and attorneys (e.g., NRC investigators, licensees, counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory text for using and interpreting Federal Register documents (how they are organized and cited) and for agency procedural rules (ex: NRC witness sequestration/exclusion, FAR debarment and VE cost rules). Useful for researching regulations, preparing comments, or advising regulated parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register briefing topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefings present: (1) the regulatory process with focus on the Federal Register system and the public’s role in development of regulations; (2) the relationship between the Federal Register and Code of Federal Regulations; (3) the important elements of typical Federal Register documents; (4) an introduction to the finding aids of the FR/CFR system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide the public with access to information necessary to research Federal agency regulations that affect them; no discussion of specific agency regulations in these briefings. (Includes reservation/contact info for briefing.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register purpose and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register provides a uniform system for making available to the public regulations and legal notices issued by Federal agencies, including Presidential proclamations and Executive Orders and documents of general applicability and legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents are on file for public inspection the day before publication unless earlier filing requested. How to cite: use volume number and page number (example: 55 FR 12345). There are no restrictions on republication of material appearing in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of sequestration/exclusion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule applies to all interviews under subpoena within the jurisdiction of the NRC other than those which focus on NRC employees or its contractors; it does not apply to subpoenas issued pursuant to 10 CFR 2.720.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although often discussed with reference to licensees and licensee counsel, the rule is equally applicable to non-licensees whose activities fall within the Commission's jurisdiction, and to inspections/investigations conducted by NRC officials generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and purpose of sequestration
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequestration is intended as the act of separating or isolating persons during agency interviews (analogous to the common meaning and to Federal Rule of Evidence 615).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term clarified in final rule; in this context 'exclusion' is the proper term for removing counsel. Purpose: discourage fabrication, inaccuracy and collusion during investigative interviews to preserve integrity of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of counsel representing multiple interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may exclude counsel for a subpoenaed witness when that counsel represents multiple interests and there is a reasonable basis to believe such representation will prejudice, impede, or impair the integrity of the inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple representation alone is not sufficient; exclusion is warranted where the investigating official concludes counsel's presence will impair the investigation. Examples include counsel who states intent to report employee interview contents to the licensee, potentially chilling candor and impeding fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and procedural safeguards before exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigating official is required to consult with the Office of the General Counsel before exercising exclusion authority; the final rule includes additional procedural safeguards governing the exclusion process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural mechanisms and responsibilities are meant to avoid ad hoc resolution and to notify affected persons of Commission policy and available processes when exclusion authority is exercised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for exclusion: 'reasonable basis' (not 'concrete evidence')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission uses a 'reasonable basis' standard to support exclusion of counsel rather than the stricter 'concrete evidence' standard articulated in SEC v. Csapo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification: NRC investigations implicate public health and safety, and waiting for 'concrete evidence' that an investigation has been impeded could be unacceptably risky; thus a less exacting standard is appropriate to allow prompt administrative remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on exercise of exclusion authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion authority is intended to be confined to the most compelling cases; the mere fact of multiple representation does not automatically warrant exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is intended to be used sparingly; historical experience shows only limited cases would have warranted exclusion, and the Commission intends the remedy to be narrowly applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing right to counsel of choice with investigatory integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule recognizes that exclusion may burden a witness's choice of counsel but does not deprive the right to counsel; the right to a particular counsel may be circumscribed where broader societal interests in effective administration and investigatory integrity are implicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative (civil) investigatory contexts differ from criminal proceedings; standards for appointment/effective assistance under the Sixth Amendment do not directly apply. The Commission believes alternative qualified counsel will generally be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for determining a reasonable time to obtain substitute counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes a 'reasonable period of time' for a witness to retain replacement counsel must be determined case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include availability of experienced counsel for the witness, complexity of the case, need for counsel to familiarize with facts, and the Commission’s need to conclude an investigation promptly to protect public health and safety. The one-week example in the proposal is illustrative, not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequestration's relation to First Amendment concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule's sequestration provisions are reasonably related to the NRC's fact-finding function and do not, by terms or intended application, prohibit communications or associational rights of witnesses before or after interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequestration is narrowly aimed at preventing collusion/fabrication during interviews and is no more restrictive of First Amendment rights than Federal Rule of Evidence 615.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale: disclosure to licensee can impede investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: When counsel representing both licensee and employee discloses interview content to the licensee, employees may be chilled from candidly providing information, thereby impairing the NRC's fact-finding mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule responds to real instances where disclosure by counsel impeded investigations; protection and nondisclosure of investigative information can be necessary to avoid warning suspects or other witnesses and to prevent thwarting the inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of listing (debarment/suspension) — prohibited agency actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors who are debarred, suspended, or proposed for debarment are excluded from conducting business with the Government as prime contractors, subcontractors, or as agents or representatives; agencies shall not, unless written compelling reason, take certain actions with these parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited actions include: (1) solicit offers; (2) award contracts; (3) consent to subcontracts; (4) enter into or place orders against basic agreements/basic ordering agreements/similar agreements; (5) place orders exceeding guaranteed minimum under indefinite quantity contracts; (6) when optional user, place orders against schedule contracts; (7) place orders under any other agreement that does not legally bind the Government to acquire supplies or services. Exceptions require written determination of compelling reason (see cited FAR provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation and limitation of current contracts after debarment
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding debarment/suspension/proposed debarment, performance may continue under contracts/subcontracts/agreements existing at the time unless the head of the agency directs otherwise; agencies shall not exercise options, renew, or extend current contracts with debarred/suspended contractors unless the agency head states in writing compelling reasons to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision on termination action should follow review by contracting, technical personnel and counsel to ensure propriety. See FAR 9.405-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of value engineering change proposal (VECP) costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor costs associated with developing and submitting value engineering change proposals (VECPs) — including costs for unaccepted VECPs — are allowable or unallowable as determined in accordance with FAR part 31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAR 48.101(b) clarifies there are two VE approaches: (1) an incentive voluntary approach where contractor uses its own resources to develop VECPs and sharing of savings occurs when accepted; allowability of development/implementation costs is determined under part 31. This clarifies prior confusion that such costs were per se unallowable.
